extracted.intended_audience: Python users, educators, or creators who want to make mathematical animations with Manim
extracted.subtask_description: A beginner-oriented tutorial for making mathematical animations in Python using the Manim engine (by 3Blue1Brown), covering installation, basic scene/code structure, text and equation rendering, 2D/3D graphing, and Jupyter usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation (follow Manim docs)
rubrics_metrics.description: For installing Manim on your system, I recommend following the Installation guide from the Manim documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official installation guide; check the 'Optional Dependencies' section for extra tools (e.g., LaTeX). The post links to the Manim documentation and community repositories for setup details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command-line rendering and flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Run manim from the command line to render scenes (example: manim square_to_circle.py SquareToCircle -p -ql).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example flags: -p to preview, -ql for quick/low quality. Use the module/script name and the Scene class name to render specific scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import style: from manim import *
rubrics_metrics.description: Importing everything using the * operator is the recommended way of using Manim, as a single script often uses multiple names from the Manim namespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a top-level from manim import * to avoid repetitive imports; the article explicitly recommends this pattern for typical scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene class and construct method
rubrics_metrics.description: For running animations, you have to create a class that inherits from Manim's Scene class. Inside the class, you need to create the construct method. The construct method is essentially the main method for the class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write all animation code inside construct(self). The Scene subclass + construct pattern is the canonical structure for Manim animations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating and showing MObjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Create shape MObjects (e.g., Circle(), Square()) and display them using the play method with animation constructors like Create, Transform, FadeOut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example sequence: create objects, then self.play(Create(square)), self.play(Transform(square, circle)), self.play(FadeOut(square)). Use Create to add, Transform to morph, FadeOut to remove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifying object appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify MObjects using methods like flip, rotate, and set_fill to change orientation, rotation, color, and opacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: square.flip(RIGHT); square.rotate(-3*TAU/8); circle.set_fill(PINK, opacity=0.5). Apply these before playing animations so the displayed object has the desired appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displaying text with Text objects
rubrics_metrics.description: To display text, you need to create a Text object and pass it the text you want to write to the screen. After that, you can display the text using the play method and some animation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create multiple Text objects for different lines, position with next_to (e.g., second_line.next_to(first_line, DOWN)), use Write and ReplacementTransform to animate text, and use self.wait(seconds) to control timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positioning text (next_to, to_corner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Position Text (and other mobjects) relative to each other using methods like next_to and to_corner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use next_to(first_line, DOWN) to place lines beneath each other; for fixed frame HUD text in 3D scenes use to_corner(UL) and add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing control with wait
rubrics_metrics.description: Use self.wait(n) calls to pause the scene for n seconds to control pacing of animations and transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert self.wait(1), self.wait(2), etc., between plays to create readable timing and pauses for viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rendering math with LaTeX via Tex objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Math equations can be written in Manim using LaTeX. Instead of using a Text object for equations, you need to use a Tex object. When making an equation, you need to put a $ at the start and end of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: equation = Tex(r'$d(p,q)=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(q_i-p_i)^2}$'). Note: to use LaTeX you must have a LaTeX distribution (e.g., TeX Live) installed; see 'Optional Dependencies' in installation guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using LaTeX symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: You can add symbols like the summation or integral symbols with backslash commands inside Tex strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard LaTeX syntax inside Tex(...) strings; prefix raw strings r'...' to avoid Python escaping issues (e.g., Tex(r'$\\alpha$') for α).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating 2D graphs with Axes and plot
rubrics_metrics.description: To create a graph, create an Axes object (specifying x_range, y_range, axis_config), then call axes.plot with a function (lambda or other callable) which returns y for each x to produce a plot mobject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: axes = Axes(x_range=[-3,3], y_range=[-5,5], axis_config={'color': BLUE}); graph = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, color=WHITE); label via axes.get_graph_label(graph, label='x^{2}'). Display with Create(axes), Create(graph), Write(graph_label).

rubrics_metrics.name: Animating graph transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Transform to morph one graph into another and update labels accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: self.play(Transform(graph, graph2), Transform(graph_label, graph_label2)) to animate change from x^2 to x^3.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3D scenes: inherit ThreeDScene and set camera
rubrics_metrics.description: To create a 3D graph, inherit from the ThreeDScene class. Use ThreeDAxes and set_camera_orientation to control the 3D camera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: class threeDGraph(ThreeDScene): ... self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75*DEGREES, theta=30*DEGREES). Add axes and other mobjects; use add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects for overlay text in fixed screen positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding and fixing mobjects in frame
rubrics_metrics.description: Use self.add(...) to add mobjects to the scene and add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects(...) to add objects that should remain fixed relative to the screen (e.g., HUD text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 3D scenes where scene objects rotate with camera, use add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects for UI/text that should not rotate. Use to_corner(UL) to position fixed elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using %%manim Jupyter magic
rubrics_metrics.description: Manim ships with a %%manim IPython magic command, which allows you to use Manim inside JupyterLab / Jupyter Notebooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the %%manim cell magic in notebooks to render Manim scenes inline. See corresponding documentation for examples and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lambda or callable for plot functions
rubrics_metrics.description: To specify a graph you need a method that returns a y value for every x; lambda functions are convenient but any callable works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass the function to axes.plot; lambdas are shown in examples but you can define named functions if preferred for readability or complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage code-based reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating animations using code makes things reproducible and easy to change compared to manual video editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tutorial emphasizes that code-driven animation workflows improve reproducibility and ease of iteration; prefer programmatic animation for repeatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult community resources and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to community repositories and tutorials (e.g., ManimCommunity/manim, Manim-Tutorial) for more examples and deeper learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post links to GitHub repos and additional tutorials; use these for extended examples, patterns, and community-contributed utilities.
